text:
anya: Heads-up — ran a profiler on the G4 cluster this morning. Seeing a sharp OOM cliff when the continuous-batcher forms groups of >=6 requests and average KV tokens per request is ~120k. Memory climbs steadily then device OOM and a slow fallback to the CPU kernel (~800-1k ms).

sam: Can you drop the flamegraph / perf link? :thinking_face:

anya: Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/scan/abc123 (private). Key log excerpt below:
```
[2026-02-12T09:12:41Z] batcher: forming batch id=542 size=7 est_tokens=840000 kv_headroom_left=0.03
[2026-02-12T09:12:41Z] runtime: kernel-selector chose=fused-attn device=GPU0
[2026-02-12T09:12:42Z] runtime ERROR: device OOM while allocating kv cache (requested 1.4GB)
[2026-02-12T09:12:43Z] runtime: fallback-to-cpu-kernel delay=921ms
[2026-02-12T09:12:43Z] batcher: batch id=542 failed oom; tracing attached
```

leo: Does the batcher respect kv_headroom_pct before admitting more requests? What config did this run use?

anya: We were on kv_headroom_pct=0.05 (legacy). Also max_batch_tokens=4096, token_budget_target=512. I tried bumping kv_headroom_pct to 0.20 locally — stops the OOM but throughput drops ~12% (fewer coalesced requests).

maria: Two ideas: (1) early admission precheck to predict "long-prefix" requests (route them to a memory-conservative pool or smaller batch size); (2) kernel-selector guard: if kv_miss_rate or predicted kv_writes are high, prefer memory-friendly kernel even if fused-attn is faster in the microbench.

sam: This smells like the kernel-selector refactor from r2334 — it now prefers fused-attn for most shapes. I repro'd locally: reverting the selector change reduces these OOMs. The selector currently doesn't account for KV footprint variance.

anya: Repro script I used:
```
./tools/repro_batch_kv.sh --model redwood-13b --batch 8 --kv-avg 120000 --seed 42
# output snippet:
# batch 8 total_tokens=960k kv_headroom_left=0.02 -> OOM on GPU
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary r2334 detected regressions; auto-rollback initiated at 2678901250.

leo: Proposed plan:
- bump default kv_headroom_pct to 0.18 in canary config (quick mitigation)
- add admission precheck: if predicted_batch_kv_tokens + current_kv_usage > kv_capacity * (1 - kv_headroom_pct) then reject/admit to separate queue
- kernel-selector patch: add kv_miss_rate threshold (>=0.6) to prefer memory-conservative kernels and avoid large fused kernels when KV cache heavy
I'll open a PR with small changes and perf tests.

anya: I'll run a 48h trace replay with mixed traffic and measure headroom_utilization, kv_miss_rate, and p95 latency. I'll also add those metrics to the console per-route panel so we can see admission decisions in real time.

sam: :thumbsup: Owners: leo -> PR (kernel + admission), anya -> trace + dashboard, sam -> canary rollout verification. Let's avoid wide rollout until we validate throughput impact.

maria: One more note — we should add a small fast path that computes a cheap "kv_token_estimate" at enqueue time (prefix_len * kv_token_per_token_est) so batching can make better packing decisions without inflating headroom risk.
